PullRequest.Title: agentHost: Resolve published MCP server lifecycle IDs
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #332072

## Problem

Agent Host start/stop handling reverse-resolved customization IDs only through the controller's runtime `_live` inventory. During a same-name collision, the runtime can first associate a server name with a published plugin child and then receive a distinct same-name workspace top-level customization.

Agent Customizations presents the workspace entry and sends its exact ID, but the live lookup no longer recognizes that ID. The provider logs `Cannot start unknown MCP server customization ...`, no server process starts, and the optimistic client reducer leaves the row at `Starting`.

## Change

Keep the runtime lookup as the first choice, then fall back to an exact-ID lookup across the session's currently published customizations.

The fallback accepts only an ID that is present in current session state. It does not add a broad same-name alias and does not change collision precedence. The SDK lifecycle API remains name-keyed, so it starts the effective server winner already selected for that name.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client`
- `npx mocha test/unit/node/index.js --delay --ui=tdd --timeout=20000 --exit --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/shared/mcpCustomizationController.test.ts` — 20 passing
- Targeted ESLint and `git diff --check`
- Regression coverage verifies published IDs resolve before the SDK has populated the live inventory and unknown IDs remain rejected.
- Deterministic live Code OSS A/B with a real Copilot Agent Host session and real local stdio MCP processes:
  - A host-only plugin published and started `dupe`; the real UI then stopped it through its plugin-child customization ID.
  - A workspace-root `.mcp.json` with another `dupe` was published afterward, producing two distinct current customization IDs with no synthetic `mcp-top-level:*` ID and no intervening SDK state event that could repair the mapping.
  - Unpatched main: the UI dispatched `SessionMcpServerStartRequested` with the exact workspace ID, Agent Host logged the matching unknown-customization warning, no process spawned, and the clicked row remained stuck at `Starting`.
  - Patched: the UI dispatched the same workspace ID, no unknown-customization warning was logged, a new real MCP process spawned, the workspace entry transitioned `stopped -> starting -> ready`, and the clicked row reached `Running`.
  - A separate `solo` server completed stop/start successfully as a control.
- The patched live arm was repeated through the repository's normal `scripts/code.bat` launch path with the same result.

Current source combines user and `.vscode/mcp.json` inputs before Agent Host receives them, so the live harness used a host-configured plugin child plus workspace-root `.mcp.json` to deterministically reproduce the same published child/top-level identity collision described by the issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot MCP start/stop for a customization already represented in the controller's live inventory
Scenarios.CriticalPath: UI lifecycle action reaches AgentSideEffects, CopilotAgent, then serverNameForCustomizationId; the existing live-map loop resolves the ID and the SDK lifecycle RPC is queued. The new session-state fallback is not reached, so no changed work is on this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot SDK mcp.startServer, mcp.stopServer, and post-start state reconciliation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lifecycle RPC per accepted user action, serialized per server; reconciliation follows start as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same live-ID action resolved and invoked the same queued SDK lifecycle RPC before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The SDK RPC is the dominant asynchronous lifecycle work after ID resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live MCP servers scanned by the pre-existing lookup; one lookup per explicit start/stop action.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Copilot serializes lifecycle operations per server through SequencerByKey; different servers may proceed independently. The diff does not alter this scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The live observable map is the fast path on both cold and warm calls; successful live matches bypass the new fallback. No negative cache exists, but it is irrelevant for valid live IDs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: control flow returns from the unchanged live scan before the added lines.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact live-server counts and RPC duration vary, but the changed fallback is provably bypassed for this scenario.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the common live-inventory lifecycle path has no changed performance behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot MCP start/stop for a currently published customization missing from the live SDK inventory
Scenarios.CriticalPath: UI lifecycle action performs an in-memory session-state lookup, flattens current MCP customizations, and scans for the exact ID; on a match it queues one SDK start/stop RPC. The O(C) flatten-and-find runs synchronously before the RPC, where C is current top-level customizations plus children.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot SDK starts or stops the resolved MCP server; start then seeds current server states from the SDK
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One queued lifecycle RPC per user action; no per-customization boundary fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the fallback, this valid published ID was rejected and no lifecycle RPC or server process start/stop occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The RPC/process lifecycle is required for the requested action and dominates the small in-memory lookup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All currently published customization containers and children in one session; effective frequency is one fallback scan per explicit lifecycle action that misses the live inventory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Lookup is synchronous and single-shot. Accepted Copilot lifecycle calls remain serialized per server by SequencerByKey, preventing same-server bursts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A subsequently live server returns through the existing live fast path. The fallback deliberately reads current session state rather than retaining a stale cache; unknown IDs repeat the bounded scan.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added line invokes findMcpServerName, which allocates and scans a flattened MCP list, and a match newly reaches the established RPC path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Customization counts can vary, but realistic session inventories are bounded and lifecycle clicks are infrequent; no evidence shows the linear temporary array is material at those cardinalities.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the bounded O(C) lookup and single serialized boundary call are necessary to restore the explicitly requested lifecycle operation, without repeated fan-out or hot-path execution.

Scenarios.Scenario: Codex MCP start for a published customization not resolved by the refreshed live inventory, including an unmaterialized session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The lifecycle request refreshes the controller from in-memory inventory, then the new fallback scans current session customizations. A match may materialize the Codex thread, issue one configuration reload IPC, and page through MCP status IPC responses before the action completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize or resume the Codex thread connection when needed
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one materialization/resume sequence for the accepted lifecycle request; already-materialized sessions reuse their connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: For the affected valid published-but-not-live ID, resolution returned undefined and this boundary was not reached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before MCP configuration reload can run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send config/mcpServer/reload to the Codex app server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one reload request per accepted start action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The broken ID path returned before issuing reload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required lifecycle boundary on the action's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List full MCP server status with cursor pagination
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: P sequential requests per accepted start, determined by status-list pagination; not one request per server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No inventory refresh occurred when the valid published ID was rejected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after reload and must complete before startMcpServer resolves.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fallback scan over session customizations, followed by one reload and P status-list requests where P is the server-status pagination count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new limiter is introduced in Codex, but normal UI state transitions make this one operation per explicit click; no realistic changed trigger establishes a concurrent burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing inventory/live entries remain the fast path after refresh. The fallback uses authoritative current session state; the subsequent status refresh replaces the in-memory inventory for future calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for reachability and boundary count; lower prevalence because the fallback only matters when live inventory cannot already resolve the published ID.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Thread materialization and pagination latency vary, but each is bounded to an explicit start request and no evidence shows accidental repetition or fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: the newly reachable IPC work is the intended bounded implementation of the previously rejected start action, not redundant work or an amplified hot path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Lifecycle request carrying an unknown customization ID
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the unchanged live scan misses, the added code reads in-memory session state, flattens MCP entries, scans them, and returns undefined; callers log and stop before any SDK or process boundary.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: O(C) CPU and temporary references for C MCP customizations per invalid lifecycle action.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous work on action handling; no downstream asynchronous operation is started.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unknown IDs are not negatively cached, so repeated invalid actions rescan current state; no normal product workflow generates a high-frequency stream of invalid lifecycle IDs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: findMcpServerName flattens and scans, then callers return before lifecycle RPCs.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A malicious or defective client could repeat invalid actions, but that is not a realistic trigger evidenced by this diff and the per-action inventory is bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: one bounded scan per invalid explicit action is insufficient to establish actionable CPU/GC impact.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced the added fallback through Copilot and Codex lifecycle callers, in-memory state access, allocation/cardinality, sequencing, thread materialization, SDK/app-server IPC, and inventory pagination. The only new synchronous cost is a bounded linear flatten-and-find on live-map misses; newly reachable expensive boundaries are the requested start/stop work for IDs that were previously rejected. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
